Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Nexus Utilities Corp. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during listen-only portions of the call. To ask a question, you will need to retrieve your handset and press the star key followed by the 1 key at that time. To withdraw your question, press the star key followed by the 2 key. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Thompson: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Nexus Utilities Corp.'s Q2 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Mike Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Reynolds, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer, and David Patel, Chief Strategy Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Harlan.

Mike Harlan: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by:
    1. Strong operational performance in our generation fleet.
    2. Continued growth in our renewable energy portfolio.
    3. Effective cost management.
    4. Progress on our infrastructure investments.
    5. Successful integration of our recently acquired 600 MW wind farm from Invenergy.

Let me provide some more detail on these five key aspects. Starting with our operational strength, our 25 GW diversified fleet across natural gas combined-cycle plants, nuclear assets, wind farms, and solar-plus-storage projects demonstrated remarkable resilience. We hit a system-wide equivalent availability factor of 93.2%, the best Q2 in five years, bolstered by proactive maintenance on our 4 GW nuclear fleet at Prairie Island and Monticello. Renewables growth included commissioning the first 150 MW of the Desert Sun solar-plus-storage project in Arizona, with 100 MWh of Tesla Megapack batteries delivering dispatchable clean energy and $15 million in ancillary services from CAISO. Electrification trends advanced with 1.2 GW of PPAs from hyperscalers like AWS and Microsoft, worth $1.8 billion through 2035. Cost controls shone through O&M down 8% per MWh to $22.50 via digital twins on GE Vernova's Predix platform, cutting unplanned outages 25%, and $45 million in fuel savings from hedging at $2.85/MMBtu Henry Hub. Regionally, MISO South retail grew 11%, ERCOT gas plants captured $120 million in scarcity uplifts. We added 450 MW wind with Ørsted, hitting 35% renewables penetration, and invested $300 million in hydrogen blending at Mystic CC.

On renewables expansion, our contracted backlog reached 8 GW with 92% fixed-price to investment-grade off-takers, while merchant exposure stayed disciplined at 15%. Cost management kept EBITDA margins strong amid weather and regulatory pressures. Infrastructure progress included transmission upgrades and smart grid rollouts, with capex focused on wheeling data center loads. The Invenergy acquisition is delivering 9% IRR immediately.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Reynolds to discuss the financials in more depth.

Sarah Reynolds: Thank you, Mike. Good morning, everyone. For the Q2, we reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.45 and revenue of $2.85 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $650 million, primarily focused on renewables integration and grid modernization efforts like transmission upgrades in SPP and solar-plus-storage projects. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders. We anticipate full-year adjusted EPS of $5.70 to $6.00.

To give you fuller context on how we navigated the quarter, let me dive deeper into our key achievements and challenges. Consolidated revenues hit $2.85 billion, up 12% year-over-year, powered by 9% higher retail MWh sales to 28.2 million amid strong load growth. Adjusted EBITDA rose 15% to $825 million, margins up 220 basis points to 29%, thanks to $1.2 billion from regulated utilities and better spark spreads averaging $45/MWh in PJM and ERCOT peaks. Operationally flawless, with nuclear at 92.8% capacity factor post-refueling, renewables commissioning delivering ancillary revenue, hyperscaler PPAs positioning us for AI demand surges, O&M efficiencies via Predix digital twins, fuel hedging savings, Midwest industrial rebound, ERCOT scarcity captures, net-zero IRP progress with Ørsted wind and hydrogen pilots. Challenges included gas price pressures from Freeport LNG outage widening ISO-NE basis to $1.20/MMBtu, shaving $30 million EBITDA despite 85% hedges; Southwest heat dome wear costing $25 million in transformer fixes; cooler Midwest trimming sales 2%; FERC Order 2023 delays pushing PJM queue six months; polysilicon shortages inflating Nevada solar capex $50 million; California carbon proposals adding $18 million; capex overruns to 7% from AFUDC delays and labor inflation; ERCOT stress and Northeast coal write-downs of $100 million. Yet our 65% regulated/contracted revenues provided insulation, with storage expansions and EV tailwinds offsetting. Q3 EBITDA guided $850-900 million, liquidity at $4.5 billion.

Shifting to our dividend policy and payout ratio strategy, which anchors our capital allocation, we've maintained a 28-year dividend streak and 18 years of increases. Our Board just approved a 5% hike to $0.55 quarterly, or $2.20 annualized, with 5-year CAGR 4.2% and 10-year 5.1%, yielding 3.8% versus sector 3.2%. We target 65-75% payout of adjusted earnings, Q2 at 70.5% TTM on $0.78 EPS, aided by thermal dispatches. This balances $4.2 billion FY24 capex for clean transition—800 MW solar-storage, 200 MWh BESS, green hydrogen—retaining 25-35% for growth, aiming net debt/EBITDA 3.8x. Flexed lower in crises like WECC freezes for resiliency, higher on ERCOT spikes. Stable at 70-72% through 2025 on 6-8% EPS growth, California community solar countering NEM 3.0, PNW hydro recovery. Hybrid model like NextEra blends yield/growth, outperforming Treasuries with 1.75x FCF coverage.

Before moving on, I'd like to highlight our grid modernization and smart grid initiatives, central to growth. This $2.8 billion program delivered $450 million Q3 capex, YTD $1.2 billion toward $2.5 billion FY target, up 15%, 85% rate base-funded plus $320 million IIJA grants including $150 million EV hardening. AMI rollout hit 4.2 million smart meters, 92% urban coverage, saving $85 million Opex via 28% fewer visits, 40% less disputes, curtailing 1.2 GW peak for $45 million PJM/MISO credits. ADMS live 75% territory, SAIDI down 22% to 85 minutes, SAIFI 18% to 0.9, FLISR cutting switching 65%, avoiding $120 million penalties. DERMS aggregates 850 MW into VPPs, offsetting 450 MWh purchases for $28 million at $650/MWh NEM, with 200 MW utility BESS mitigating duck curve at 45% renewables penetration. Cybersecurity: $180 million NERC upgrades, zero incidents. Electrification: 150k Level 2/500 DC chargers, 800 MW off-peak shift, 2.5% load CAGR from EVs/data centers/manufacturing, microgrids at 15 sites for 99.999% uptime. Returns: 9.5% ROE, 5.2-year payback, $220 million Opex savings, $180 million revenue uplift. Q4 $700 million capex for ADMS Phase 2, 1 million AMI; 15% 2025 EPS contribution to $4.85-5.05.

Finally, on regulatory rate case filings and outcomes, we've covered 85% of our $28 billion rate base in past 12 months, aligning with $15 billion 5-year capex split 40/30/30 T&D/renewables/tech. ICC black-box settlement: $385 million of $450 million ask on $12.5 billion base for Prairie Wind solar/BESS, 9.75% ROE, MYRP for $3.2 billion capex including electrolyzers, $0.15-0.20 EPS 2025 uplift, 4.2% bill impact. PUCO full $320 million approval at 10.25% ROE for T&D resiliency, EV rider. Georgia PSC $240 million of $280 million at 10.0% ROE with IRA flow-through. Pending: Indiana $520 million largest ever at 10.50% ROE for Hoosier Grid/AMI; Missouri $190 million for coal retirement/gas peakers. Targeting 9.8-10.3% ROEs, FERC incentives; trends like clean mandates, data centers fueling growth. Average 11-month lag, 75% settlements support $2.95-3.05 EPS, 7% dividend growth.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Sarah. Let me provide an update on the operational front. We are seeing improved efficiency in our natural gas combined-cycle power plants due to the implementation of digital twin technology from GE Vernova's Predix platform. This has resulted in a 15% increase in output, alongside 25% fewer unplanned outages across our 10 GW gas fleet and enhanced hydro refurbishments for relicensing.

David Patel: Thank you, Lisa. Turning to our long-term strategy, we are actively exploring opportunities in the battery energy storage systems and small modular reactors space, including our LOI with NuScale for four 77 MW modules at a retired coal site, 1,200 MW BESS pipeline, and offshore bids with Siemens Gamesa.

Mike Harlan: Thank you, Sarah, Lisa, and David. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Julien Dumoulin-Smith with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Julien Dumoulin-Smith, BofA: Thanks, good morning everyone. Strong quarter here—congrats on the beat. But maybe drill down on the regulated segment. You guys grew revenues 12% YoY to $2.1 billion, which is ahead of your guide, but capex came in at $850 million, a bit light versus the $900 million consensus. What's the read-through on the '25 capex plan, especially with FERC's recent ROE complaints in PJM? And how does that interplay with your 1,200 MW battery pipeline?

Sarah Reynolds: Thanks, Julien. Great question on the regulated side. First off, Q2 revenues were indeed $2.1 billion, up 12% driven by 5% rate base growth and favorable weather normalization in ERCOT and MISO. The capex underspend was intentional—$850 million reflects phasing on our 500 kV transmission upgrades in the SPP footprint, where we deferred $50 million of stringing and substation work to Q4 to align with delayed permitting from the Kansas Corporation Commission. Looking to '25, we're holding the high end of our $3.6-3.8 billion guidance, with 45% allocated to renewables integration—think $1.2 billion for the 1,200 MW BESS queue we discussed. On FERC ROE, we're advocating for a 10.5% base in our PJM formula rate update, benchmarking against Duke and Dominion's recent 9.8-10.2% approvals. The formulaic adder for our 15 GW renewables fleet should push us to 10.8%, supporting 8-9% EPS growth. Batteries are key here—our 400 MW/800 MWh Pasadena project, co-located with 300 MW solar, is already in commercial ops and arbitraging ERCOT peaks at $150/MWh spreads.

Operator: Next question from David Arcaro with Morgan Stanley.

David Arcaro, MS: Hey team, thanks. On the renewables side, impressive 25% YoY growth in contracted backlog to 8 GW, but merchant exposure ticked up to 15% of the portfolio. With CAISO curtailment hitting 10% in Q2 and NatGas futures at $2.80/MMBtu, how are you thinking about hedging for the 2 GW wind repower in Texas? Any color on hyperscaler PPAs amid data center load growth?

Mike Harlan: David, spot on with the backlog—8 GW fully contracted at 15-year terms, 92% fixed-price with investment-grade off-takers like Google and Microsoft. Merchant is disciplined at 15%, hedged 80% through '26 at $45/MWh floors via financial collars. For the Texas repower—1,200 MW of Vestas V162-6.2 MW turbines replacing our legacy 1.8 MW fleet—we're targeting COD in H2 '26, leveraging IRA PTCs at $27/MWh plus bonuses for domestic content (85% U.S.-sourced). ERCOT demand is surging 18% YoY from hyperscalers; we've signed three 500 MW PPAs since Q1, including a landmark 10-year deal with Amazon at $55/MWh indexed to capacity factors above 45%. Curtailment risk? Mitigated via our 300 MW/600 MWh Hornsdale-style BESS in West Texas, shifting output to evenings for 20% uplift.

Operator: Our next question is from Neal Dingmann with Truist.

Neal Dingmann, Truist: Good morning. Solid margins—adjusted EBITDA up 14% to $1.4 billion, FFO to debt at 18%. But O&M came in higher at 22% of revenues due to hydro refurbishments. With coal retirements accelerating—your 1 GW unit offline—what's the fuel mix evolution, and any update on nuclear SMR pursuits post-Vogtle? Regional color on Southeast demand?

Sarah Reynolds: Neal, thanks. EBITDA margins held at 42%, best in class, thanks to 92% availability across our 25 GW fleet. O&M was $720 million, up 8% YoY from $30 million in hydro turbine overhauls at our 800 MW Columbia River assets—necessary for relicensing through 2040 with FERC. Fuel mix: Renewables now 55% (up from 48% last year), natgas 35%, coal down to 8% post our 1 GW Rockport retirement. Nuclear at 2% for now, but we're advancing SMRs—LOI with NuScale for four 77 MW VOYGR modules at our retired coal site in Georgia, targeting '29 ops with $1.2 billion capex offset by 45Q credits. Southeast: SERC demand +12% from EV charging and manufacturing; our 2 GW solar + storage in Georgia is 95% subscribed via Georgia Power RFPs, with weather-normalized load growth at 3.5%.

Operator: From Angie Storozynski with Morningstar.

Angie Storozynski, Morningstar: Hi all. Dividend coverage remains robust at 2.0x, but with $4.2 billion liquidity and $12 billion LT debt, how aggressive on buybacks versus M&A? Thoughts on Orsted-style offshore bids in New York Bight? And wildfire risk mitigation post-California PG&E?

Mike Harlan: Angie, strong balance sheet—net debt to EBITDA at 3.4x, investment grade across the board. Buybacks: $300 million authorized for '24, deployed $150 million YTD at $68/share. M&A priority: accretive bolt-ons like our $450 million acquisition of 600 MW wind from Invenergy in Oklahoma, 9% IRR. Offshore: We're shortlisted for 1.2 GW in NYSERDA's round, partnering with Siemens Gamesa on 15 MW Haliade-X platforms—$3/MWh bids viable with IIJA funding. Wildfire: $200 million invested in our California portfolio for covered conductors and AI-driven grid monitoring, akin to PG&E's $15 billion hardening plan. No material reserve adds needed; insurance recovery on Q1 outages was $120 million.

Operator: Final question from Stephen Byrd with Pernod Ricard Securities.

Stephen Byrd, Pernod Ricard Securities: Quick one on guidance. '24 adjusted EPS midpoint $5.85, implying 7% growth. Sensitivities to gas prices or load? And strategic read-through from EIA's 4.2% U.S. demand forecast?

Sarah Reynolds: Stephen, guidance firm at $5.70-6.00. Gas sensitivity: 90% hedged '24-'25 at $3.00/MMBtu cap; $1/MMBtu rise shaves 2 cents EPS. Load: +1% drives 3 cents. EIA's 4.2% is bullish—our scenarios pencil 5-6% from data centers (1 GW contracted) and electrification. We're positioned with 3 GW queued renewables + 1 GW dispatchable peakers for '25-27.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Mike Harlan for closing remarks.

Mike Harlan: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the Q2, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Nexus Utilities Corp. for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Nexus Utilities Corp.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
